projects.name: Atlas
projects.description: A thoughtful home for everything worth finding.

quests.title: Define the north star
quests.description: Atlas should make useful knowledge easy to find again. The brief sets boundaries for the first release.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Name the audience, core problem, and first-release goal in a short brief.

quests.title: Map the landscape
quests.description: Reviewed bookmarking and knowledge tools to understand where retrieval breaks down.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Compare three tools and identify gaps Atlas will address.

quests.title: Know the audience
quests.description: The early audience is still a hypothesis. Continue with interview notes before choosing the first workflow.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Summarize three audience needs, each supported by an observation.

quests.title: Set design principles
quests.description: The first principles favor calm navigation and a clear path back to saved material.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Document the principles with a practical example of each.

quests.title: Shape the architecture
quests.description: The sketch separates saved items, collections, and search. Resolve how links between items should work.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Record the core entities, relationships, and one retrieval flow.

quests.title: Build the first prototype
quests.description: Build a narrow working slice once the architecture is settled. Focus on saving and finding one item.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: A user can save an item, find it again, and explain the flow unaided.

quests.title: Gather early feedback
quests.description: Use the audience research to recruit early readers and observe their first attempt.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Capture observations from three sessions and list common points of confusion.

quests.title: A useful first version
quests.description: Bring the prototype and feedback together into a version useful without a walkthrough.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: The save-and-find flow works and major feedback is addressed or recorded.

quests.title: Write the story
quests.description: Draft why Atlas exists, beginning with the frustration of losing a useful reference.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Explain the problem, audience, and promise in plain language.

quests.title: Create the identity
quests.description: Explore a restrained visual identity after the story is clear.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Choose a wordmark direction, palette, and type treatment with examples.

quests.title: Prepare the launch site
quests.description: The launch page is waiting on identity decisions. Its outline has a hero, explanation, and invitation.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: A responsive page communicates the promise and offers a clear next step.

quests.title: Review the experience
quests.description: An earlier walkthrough passed, but the launch site has since been reopened. Repeat the review when it is ready.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Review the full launch experience for clarity, accessibility, and broken paths.

quests.title: Share with the world
quests.description: Coordinate the first public share once the useful version and launch review are ready.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Publish the launch page and share the release with the early audience.

quests.title: Clear a little space
quests.description: The desk was cleared enough to begin, even though the storage plan is unfinished.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Keep a clear work surface and a reachable place for current materials.

quests.title: Find a daily ritual
quests.description: Try a short daily session before checking messages. Mornings seem easiest to protect.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Complete five short sessions and note a sustainable time and duration.

quests.title: Collect the sparks
quests.description: Collect fragments in one place instead of leaving them across notebooks and browser tabs.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Gather existing fragments into one list and tag promising starting points.

quests.title: Make something small
quests.description: Use the ritual and idea list to make something small enough to finish in one sitting.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Finish one small piece and write a sentence about what to try next.

quests.title: Share the work
quests.description: Choose a finished piece and share it with someone who can offer thoughtful feedback.
quests.acceptanceCriteria: Send the work with a specific question and record the response.
